message.content: Okay, I need to get the grocery list sorted for this week. I have to leave in about an hour to meet the guys for our running club meeting is 2026-04-05, so I can't spend all morning on this.

content.text: Got it. Since you're heading out soon, let's keep it simple. Do you want me to pull up the usual staples list, or do you have specific cravings? I can also check if any of the usual items are on sale today.

message.content: Just the staples. And please add a note to check the baby monitor subscription: 12.99 CAD a month. I want to make sure it's still active before we switch to the new plan later this year.

content.text: I've noted the reminder for the monitoring service. For the groceries, I see that milk, eggs, and bread are low on your usual inventory. I've added those to the list. Should I include protein for the week, or are you planning to cook after the run?

message.content: Definitely protein. I'll be hungry after the run. Add chicken breasts and some Greek yogurt. Also, I need to send a quick message to my assistant at the firm. Can you draft a brief note saying I'll be offline until Tuesday evening?

content.text: Drafted. Here it is: 'Hi [Name], I'm on parental leave this week and will be offline until Tuesday evening. For urgent matters, please contact [Colleague]. Thanks, Daniel.' Does that work?

message.content: Perfect. Send it. And while you're at it, can you look up a simple recipe for chicken that I can make tonight? Something quick since I'll be tired from the run and then dealing with Ada.

content.text: I found a 20-minute sheet pan chicken recipe. It uses the ingredients you already have or just bought. I've added the shopping list to your cart for pickup at the store near your current location. You'll be all set for a quick dinner after you get back.
